title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Persons with Disabilities

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution for the purpose of safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, developing undertakings for persons with disabilities, and ensuring their equal and full participation in social life and their share of the material and cultural achievements of society.

Article 2 A person with a disability refers to a person who, due to the loss or abnormality of certain tissues or functions in psychology, physiology or human body structure, has lost, wholly or in part, the ability to engage in certain activities in a normal way.
Persons with disabilities include those with visual disabilities, hearing disabilities, speech disabilities, physical disabilities, intellectual disabilities, mental disabilities, multiple disabilities and other disabilities.
The criteria for disability shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 3 Persons with disabilities shall enjoy equal rights with other citizens in political, economic, cultural, social and family life.
The civil rights and personal dignity of persons with disabilities shall be protected by law.
Discrimination on the basis of disability shall be prohibited. Insulting or infringing upon persons with disabilities shall be prohibited. Disparaging or impairing the dignity of persons with disabilities through mass media or other means shall be prohibited.

Article 4 The State shall adopt auxiliary methods and supportive measures to provide special assistance to persons with disabilities, to reduce or eliminate the effects of disabilities and external barriers, and to ensure the realization of their rights.

Article 5 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate undertakings for persons with disabilities into the national economic and social development plan, strengthen leadership and comprehensive coordination, include the funds for such undertakings in the fiscal budget, and establish a stable funding guarantee mechanism.
The State Council shall formulate the national program for the development of undertakings for persons with disabilities, and local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on such program, formulate development plans and annual plans for undertakings for persons with disabilities within their respective administrative areas to ensure the coordinated development of such undertakings with the economy and society.
The institutions responsible for the work concerning persons with disabilities under the people's governments at or above the county level shall take charge of organizing, coordinating, guiding and supervising the relevant departments in properly carrying out the work concerning persons with disabilities.
People's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall maintain close ties with persons with disabilities, listen to their opinions, and perform their duties in the work concerning persons with disabilities.

Article 6 The State shall adopt measures to ensure that persons with disabilities, in accordance with legal provisions, participate in the management of State affairs, economic and cultural undertakings, and social affairs through various channels and forms.
When formulating laws, regulations, rules and public policies on major issues involving the rights and interests of persons with disabilities and undertakings for persons with disabilities, the opinions of persons with disabilities and organizations of persons with disabilities shall be solicited.
Persons with disabilities and organizations of persons with disabilities shall have the right to present opinions and suggestions to State organs at all levels regarding the protection of rights and interests and the development of undertakings for persons with disabilities.

Article 7 The whole society shall promote the humanitarian spirit, and understand, respect, care for and assist persons with disabilities, and support undertakings for persons with disabilities.
The State encourages social organizations and individuals to provide donations and services to persons with disabilities.
State organs, social organizations, enterprises, public institutions and grassroots self-governing organizations in urban and rural areas shall do well in the work concerning persons with disabilities within their respective scope.
State functionaries and other persons engaged in work concerning persons with disabilities shall, according to law, perform their duties and strive to serve persons with disabilities.

Article 8 The China Disabled Persons' Federation and its local organizations shall represent the common interests of persons with disabilities, protect their lawful rights and interests, unite and educate them, and serve them.
The China Disabled Persons' Federation and its local organizations shall, in accordance with laws, regulations and their articles of association or upon entrustment by the government, carry out work concerning persons with disabilities, mobilize social forces, and develop undertakings for persons with disabilities.

Article 9 The supporter of a person with a disability must perform the duty of support.
The guardian of a person with a disability must perform the duty of guardianship, respect the ward's will, and protect the ward's lawful rights and interests.
Relatives and guardians of a person with a disability shall encourage and help the person to enhance the ability to be self-reliant.
Domestic violence against persons with disabilities shall be prohibited; maltreating or abandoning persons with disabilities shall be prohibited.

Article 10 The State encourages persons with disabilities to maintain self-respect, self-confidence, self-improvement and self-reliance, and to contribute to the construction of socialism.
Persons with disabilities shall abide by laws and regulations, fulfill their duties, observe public order, and respect social ethics.

Article 11 The State shall carry out work on disability prevention in a planned manner, strengthen leadership in disability prevention, publicize and popularize knowledge on maternal and child health care and disability prevention, establish and improve mechanisms for the prevention, early detection and early treatment of birth defects, and, regarding genetic, disease, drug, accident, disaster, environmental pollution and other factors causing disabilities, organize and mobilize social forces and adopt measures to prevent the occurrence of disabilities and reduce the degree of disability.
The State shall establish and improve the statistical survey system for persons with disabilities, and carry out the statistical survey and analysis of the situation of persons with disabilities.

Article 12 The State and society shall grant special protection, pensions and preferential treatment to disabled military personnel, persons who become disabled in the course of performing official duties, and other persons who become disabled in the course of safeguarding national and public interests.

Article 13 People's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall commend and reward persons with disabilities who have made remarkable achievements in socialist construction, and units and individuals who have made remarkable achievements in protecting the lawful rights and interests of persons with disabilities, developing undertakings for persons with disabilities, or serving persons with disabilities.
Article 14 The third Sunday of May every year shall be the National Day of Assistance for Persons with Disabilities.

Article 15 The State guarantees the right of persons with disabilities to access rehabilitation services.
People's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall adopt measures to create conditions for the rehabilitation of persons with disabilities, establish and improve the rehabilitation service system for persons with disabilities, and carry out key rehabilitation projects by stages to help persons with disabilities recover or compensate for their functions and enhance their ability to participate in social life.

Article 16 Rehabilitation work shall be based on actual conditions, combine modern rehabilitation technology with traditional Chinese rehabilitation technology; be based on community rehabilitation, with rehabilitation institutions as the backbone and families of persons with disabilities as the support; focus on rehabilitation content that is practical, easy to implement and widely beneficial, giving priority to the rescue treatment and rehabilitation of disabled children; develop science and technology that meets rehabilitation requirements, encourage independent innovation, strengthen research, development and application of new rehabilitation technologies, and provide effective rehabilitation services to persons with disabilities.

Article 17 People's governments at all levels shall encourage and support social forces to establish rehabilitation institutions for persons with disabilities.
Local people's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall organize and guide community service organizations in urban and rural areas, medical prevention and health care institutions, organizations of persons with disabilities, families of persons with disabilities and other social forces to carry out community rehabilitation work.
Educational institutions for persons with disabilities, welfare units and other institutions serving persons with disabilities shall create conditions to carry out rehabilitation training activities.
Persons with disabilities shall, under the guidance of professionals and with the assistance of relevant staff, volunteers and relatives, strive to undergo training in functions, self-care ability and labor skills.

Article 18 Local people's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall, as needed and in a planned manner, establish rehabilitation medical departments in medical institutions, establish rehabilitation institutions for persons with disabilities, and carry out rehabilitation medical treatment and training, personnel training, technical guidance, scientific research and other work.

Article 19 Medical colleges and other relevant institutions shall, in a planned manner, offer rehabilitation courses, set up relevant specialties, and train various types of rehabilitation professionals.
The government and society shall adopt various forms to provide technical training to personnel engaged in rehabilitation work; popularize rehabilitation knowledge and impart rehabilitation methods to persons with disabilities, their relatives, relevant staff and volunteers.

Article 20 The relevant government departments shall organize and support the research, production, supply and maintenance services of rehabilitation devices and assistive devices for persons with disabilities.

Article 21 The State guarantees the right of persons with disabilities to equal access to education.
People's governments at all levels shall regard education for persons with disabilities as an integral part of the national education undertaking, make unified plans, strengthen leadership, and create conditions for the education of persons with disabilities.
The government, society and schools shall adopt effective measures to address practical difficulties encountered by disabled children and adolescents in schooling, and help them complete compulsory education.
People's governments at all levels shall provide free textbooks to disabled students and students from poor families of persons with disabilities receiving compulsory education, and provide subsidies for boarding living expenses and other fees; and shall provide financial assistance to disabled students and students from poor families of persons with disabilities receiving education other than compulsory education in accordance with relevant State regulations.

Article 22 Education for persons with disabilities shall adopt the policy of combining popularization with upgrading, with the focus on popularization, guarantee compulsory education, focus on the development of vocational education, actively carry out preschool education, and gradually develop education at the senior high school level and above.

Article 24 People's governments at or above the county level shall, based on factors such as the number, distribution and type of disabilities of persons with disabilities, reasonably establish educational institutions for persons with disabilities, and encourage social forces to run schools and donate to education.

Article 25 Ordinary educational institutions shall provide education to persons with disabilities who have the ability to receive ordinary education, and provide convenience and assistance for their learning.
Ordinary primary schools and junior middle schools must admit disabled children and adolescents who can adapt to their study and life; ordinary senior middle schools, secondary vocational schools and institutions of higher learning must admit disabled candidates who meet the admission requirements prescribed by the State, and may not refuse admission on the grounds of their disability; if they refuse admission, the party or his/her relatives or guardians may request the relevant department to handle the matter, and the relevant department shall order the school to admit them.
Ordinary preschool education institutions shall admit disabled children who can adapt to their life.

Article 26 Disabled children's education institutions, disabled children's classes attached to ordinary preschool education institutions, preschool classes in special education institutions, disabled children's welfare institutions, and families of disabled children shall provide preschool education to disabled children.
Special education institutions below the junior middle school level and special education classes attached to ordinary education institutions shall provide compulsory education to disabled children and adolescents who do not have the ability to receive ordinary education.
Special education institutions at the senior high school level and above, special education classes attached to ordinary education institutions and vocational education institutions for persons with disabilities shall provide cultural education at the senior high school level and above and vocational education to eligible persons with disabilities.
Institutions providing special education shall have venues and facilities suitable for the learning, rehabilitation and living characteristics of persons with disabilities.

Article 27 The relevant government departments, the units where persons with disabilities work, and relevant social organizations shall carry out literacy, vocational training, entrepreneurship training and other adult education for persons with disabilities, and encourage persons with disabilities to become self-taught.

Article 28 The State shall, in a planned manner, establish various types of special education normal colleges and specialties at all levels, and attach special education classes in ordinary normal colleges to train and cultivate special education teachers. Ordinary normal colleges shall offer special education courses or teach relevant content so that ordinary teachers acquire necessary special education knowledge.
Special education teachers and sign language interpreters shall enjoy special education allowances.

Article 29 The relevant government departments shall organize and support the research and application of Braille and sign language, the compilation and publication of special education textbooks, and the research, production and supply of teaching aids and other auxiliary items for special education.

Article 30 The State guarantees the right of persons with disabilities to work.
People's governments at all levels shall make overall plans for the employment of persons with disabilities and create conditions for their employment.

Article 31 Employment of persons with disabilities shall adopt the policy of combining centralized and decentralized placement, adopt preferential policies and supportive and protective measures, and, through multiple channels, at multiple levels and in various forms, gradually make their employment universal, stable and reasonable.

Article 32 The government and society shall establish welfare enterprises for persons with disabilities, massage institutions for the blind and other welfare units to arrange employment for persons with disabilities in a centralized manner.

Article 33 The State implements a system of employing persons with disabilities on a proportional basis.
State organs, social organizations, enterprises, public institutions and private non-enterprise units shall, in accordance with the prescribed proportion, arrange employment for persons with disabilities, and choose suitable types of work and positions for them. If the prescribed proportion is not met, they shall fulfill their obligations to guarantee the employment of persons with disabilities in accordance with relevant State regulations. The State encourages employing units to employ persons with disabilities in excess of the prescribed proportion.
Specific measures for the employment of persons with disabilities shall be prescribed by the State Council.
Article 34 The State encourages and supports persons with disabilities to choose their own jobs and start their own businesses.

Article 35 Local people's governments at all levels and rural grassroots organizations shall organize and support rural persons with disabilities to engage in farming, aquaculture, handicrafts and other forms of production and labor.

Article 36 The State shall, according to law, grant tax preferences to employing units that meet or exceed the prescribed proportion of employment of persons with disabilities or that arrange employment for persons with disabilities in a centralized manner, and to persons with disabilities who engage in individual businesses, and shall provide support in production, operation, technology, funds, materials, venues and other aspects. The State shall exempt administrative fees from persons with disabilities who engage in individual businesses.
Local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall determine products and projects suitable for production and operation by persons with disabilities, give priority to the production or operation of welfare units for persons with disabilities, and determine certain products for exclusive production by such units based on their production characteristics.
In government procurement, priority shall be given to the purchase of products or services of welfare units for persons with disabilities under equal conditions.
Local people's governments at all levels shall develop public welfare positions suitable for the employment of persons with disabilities.
The relevant departments shall give priority to issuing business licenses to persons with disabilities who apply to engage in individual businesses.
For rural persons with disabilities engaged in various types of production and labor, the relevant departments shall provide assistance in production services, technical guidance, supply of agricultural materials, purchase and sale of agricultural and sideline products, and credit.

Article 37 Public employment service institutions established by the relevant government departments shall provide free employment services to persons with disabilities.
Employment service institutions for persons with disabilities established by the federations of persons with disabilities shall organize and provide free vocational guidance, job placement and vocational training, and provide services and assistance for the employment of persons with disabilities and for employing units to recruit persons with disabilities.

Article 38 The State protects the ownership and operational autonomy of the property of welfare units for persons with disabilities, and their lawful rights and interests shall not be infringed upon.
Discrimination against persons with disabilities shall be prohibited in recruitment, regularization, promotion, professional title evaluation, labor remuneration, welfare benefits, rest and leave, social insurance, etc.
The employer of a disabled employee shall, based on the characteristics of the disabled employee, provide appropriate labor conditions and labor protection, and transform the workplace, labor equipment and living facilities as needed.
The State shall adopt measures to protect the lawful rights and interests of blind health care and medical massage practitioners.
Article 39 The employer of a disabled employee shall provide on-the-job technical training to the disabled employee to improve his/her labor skills and technical level.
Article 40 No unit or individual may force a person with a disability to work by means of violence, threat or illegal restriction of personal freedom.

Article 41 The State guarantees the right of persons with disabilities to equal participation in cultural life.
People's governments at all levels and the relevant departments shall encourage and assist persons with disabilities to participate in various cultural, sports and recreational activities, and actively create conditions to enrich the spiritual and cultural life of persons with disabilities.

Article 42 Cultural, sports and recreational activities for persons with disabilities shall be oriented to the grassroots, integrated into public cultural life, and adapted to the different characteristics and needs of various types of persons with disabilities so that persons with disabilities can participate widely.

Article 44 The government and society shall encourage and assist persons with disabilities to engage in creative work beneficial to the people in literature, art, education, science, technology and other fields.

Article 45 The government and society shall promote mutual understanding and exchanges between persons with disabilities and other citizens, publicize the undertakings for persons with disabilities and the deeds of assisting persons with disabilities, promote the spirit of continuous self-improvement of persons with disabilities, and advocate a social atmosphere of solidarity, friendship and mutual assistance.

Article 46 The State guarantees the right of persons with disabilities to enjoy various social security benefits.
The government and society shall adopt measures to improve social security for persons with disabilities and guarantee and improve their lives.

Article 47 Persons with disabilities and their employing units shall participate in social insurance in accordance with relevant State regulations.
Grassroots self-governing organizations in urban and rural areas where persons with disabilities live, and families of persons with disabilities, shall encourage and assist persons with disabilities to participate in social insurance.
For persons with disabilities who have real difficulties in life, social insurance subsidies shall be granted in accordance with relevant State regulations.

Article 48 People's governments at all levels shall provide life, education, housing and other social assistance to persons with disabilities who have real difficulties in life through multiple channels.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall adopt other measures to ensure the basic living of families of persons with disabilities who still have particular difficulties in life after receiving the minimum subsistence allowance.
People's governments at all levels shall, in accordance with regulations, provide assistance for the basic medical care, rehabilitation services, and necessary assistive device fitting and replacement of poverty-stricken persons with disabilities.
For persons with disabilities who cannot take care of themselves, local people's governments at all levels shall, based on the situation, provide nursing subsidies.

Article 49 Local people's governments at all levels shall, in accordance with regulations, provide for persons with disabilities who have no ability to work, no supporter or whose supporter lacks the ability to support, and no source of income.
The State encourages and supports social forces to establish foster care and day care institutions for persons with disabilities.
Foster care and day care institutions for persons with disabilities and their staff shall not insult, maltreat or abandon persons with disabilities.

Article 50 People's governments at or above the county level shall, based on the actual situation, provide convenience and preferential treatment for persons with disabilities when taking public transport. Persons with disabilities may carry essential assistive devices free of charge.
Blind persons may, with valid certificates, ride on urban buses, trams, subways, ferries and other public transport free of charge. Braille mail shall be sent free of charge.
The State encourages and supports units providing telecommunications and radio and television services to grant preferential treatment to blind, hearing-impaired and speech-impaired persons.
People's governments at all levels shall gradually increase other care and assistance for persons with disabilities.

Government departments and disabled persons' organizations shall establish and improve channels for donations and services to persons with disabilities from all sectors of society, encourage and support the development of charitable undertakings for persons with disabilities, and carry out volunteer assistance to persons with disabilities and other public welfare activities.

The State and society shall take measures to gradually improve barrier-free facilities, promote barrier-free information exchange, and create a barrier-free environment for persons with disabilities to participate equally in social life.
People's governments at all levels shall make overall plans for the construction of barrier-free environments, coordinate comprehensively, and strengthen supervision and administration.

The construction and renovation of barrier-free facilities shall meet the actual needs of persons with disabilities.
New construction, reconstruction, and expansion of buildings, roads, transportation facilities, etc., shall comply with the relevant national standards for barrier-free facility engineering construction.
People's governments at all levels and relevant departments shall, in accordance with the national provisions on barrier-free facility engineering construction, gradually promote the renovation of existing facilities, and give priority to the renovation of public service facilities closely related to the daily work and life of persons with disabilities.
Barrier-free facilities shall be promptly repaired and maintained.

The State shall take measures to create conditions for barrier-free information exchange for persons with disabilities.
People's governments at all levels and relevant departments shall take measures to facilitate persons with disabilities in accessing public information.
The State and society shall research, develop, and promote information exchange technologies and products suitable for use by persons with disabilities.
Where blind persons participate in various admission examinations, professional qualification examinations, and appointment examinations organized by the State, braille test papers, electronic test papers shall be provided, or assistance shall be given by specialized staff.

Public service institutions and public places shall create conditions to provide persons with disabilities with information exchange services such as voice and text prompts, sign language, and braille, and provide priority services and auxiliary services.
Public transportation vehicles shall gradually meet the requirements for barrier-free facilities. Where conditions permit, public parking lots shall set up dedicated parking spaces for persons with disabilities.

The departments organizing elections shall provide convenience for persons with disabilities to participate in elections; where conditions permit, they shall provide braille ballots for blind persons.
The State shall encourage and support the research and development of barrier-free auxiliary equipment and barrier-free transportation vehicles.
Blind persons bringing guide dogs into and out of public places shall comply with the relevant provisions of the State.

Where the lawful rights and interests of a person with a disability are infringed upon, he or she may lodge a complaint with a disabled persons' organization, which shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of the person with a disability and have the right to request the relevant department or unit to investigate and deal with the matter. The relevant department or unit shall investigate and deal with the matter according to law and give a reply.
Where a person with a disability needs assistance in safeguarding his or her lawful rights and interests through litigation, the disabled persons' organization shall provide support.
With respect to acts infringing upon the interests of a specific group of persons with disabilities, the disabled persons' organization shall have the right to request the relevant department to investigate and deal with the matter according to law.

Where the lawful rights and interests of a person with a disability are infringed upon, he or she shall have the right to request the relevant department to handle the matter according to law, or apply to an arbitration institution for arbitration according to law, or bring a lawsuit in a People's Court according to law.
For persons with disabilities who have financial difficulties or other reasons and truly need legal aid or judicial assistance, the local legal aid institution or the People's Court shall provide assistance and provide legal aid or judicial assistance to them according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a person shirks, delays, suppresses, or fails to investigate and deal with complaints, accusations, or reports of acts infringing upon the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, or retaliates against the persons who have filed such complaints, accusations, or reports, his or her unit, the competent department, or the superior organ shall order rectification, and the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.
Where a state functionary fails to perform his or her duties according to law, fails to promptly stop acts infringing upon the rights and interests of persons with disabilities, or fails to provide necessary assistance to the victim with a disability, causing serious consequences, his or her unit or the superior organ shall give sanctions to the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a person belittles or impairs the dignity of persons with disabilities through mass media or other means, the competent departments of culture, radio, television, film, press and publication, or other relevant departments shall, within their respective functions and powers, order rectification and impose administrative penalties according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, an educational institution refuses to admit students with disabilities, or imposes additional conditions beyond the admission requirements prescribed by the State to restrict the admission of students with disabilities, the relevant competent department shall order rectification, and the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a person discriminates against persons with disabilities in the recruitment of employees or other aspects, the relevant competent department shall order rectification; a worker with a disability may bring a lawsuit in a People's Court according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a support or care institution or its staff members insult, abuse, or abandon a person with a disability, the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, an administrative penalty shall be imposed according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, the new construction, reconstruction, or expansion of buildings, roads, or transportation facilities does not comply with the relevant national standards for barrier-free facility engineering construction, or barrier-free facilities are not repaired or maintained in a timely manner, causing consequences, the relevant competent department shall handle the matter according to law.

Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, the lawful rights and interests of a person with a disability are infringed upon, if other laws or regulations provide for administrative penalties, such provisions shall prevail; if property losses or other damages are caused, civil liability shall be borne according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
This Law shall come into force as of July 1, 2008.
